decisionBasis: label-free: observation dates, the XKRX session calendar and metadata only
disclosure: The v2 rules were written AFTER v1's committed readiness record made the two source-QA defects visible (a 17-day live-freshness rejection of FDR_KS200; a raw-row invalid share for YAHOO_KS11). They are therefore not blind to source METADATA. They are blind to every historical market OUTCOME: no price value, return, drawdown, episode or future label was parsed or computed.
statements: No historical market-risk outcome was computed in this change.
No drawdown, trigger performance, false alarm, recovery cost or anatomy result was inspected.
No source was selected from future returns.
No KOSPI 200 / KOSPI composite series was spliced; no FDR / Yahoo splice; no interpolation or forward fill.
No live-freshness failure is represented as a historical data failure; the selected reference is NOT live-ready (17 days stale against the 10-day live limit).
No sealed prior study was rerun, edited or reinterpreted; v1 remains DATA_BLOCKED and unchanged.
No new external acquisition occurred; the exact bytes retained by v1 are the only source input.

No coverage, continuity or identity threshold was changed from v1; only the freshness gate was removed from historical admissibility and the invalid-share denominator became expected XKRX sessions (same 0.005 limit).
Execution is not dispatched. The one-shot historical execution needs a merged protocol and a separate explicit authorization.
whyFdrPassesV2ButFailedV1: v1 mixed LIVE operational freshness into HISTORICAL admissibility and rejected FDR_KS200 solely for STALE_LAST_DATE (last date 2026-09-17, 17 days before the 2026-10-04 acquisition, against a 10-day limit). v2 separates the concepts: every identity, coverage and continuity test v1 applied is unchanged and FDR_KS200 passed them in v1 as well (no other v1 reason was recorded for it). This is a rule correction from source metadata, not outcome tuning.
